page: Amazon Web Services i2.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 61.0 GB, providing 7.62 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 1600 GB NVMe SSD. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average to weak performance profiles. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 1619.98 and 7138.99 respectively, placing them in the average tier. PassMark CPU and memory scores also fall into the average category, with database operations registering at 3356.02. However, single-threaded performance is limited, as evidenced by a poor Geekbench single-core score of 529.0 and a poor text processing score of 1079.0. Memory bandwidth is mixed, showing average speeds of 40.1 GB/sec for large block reads but weak speeds of 19.3 GB/sec for large block writes.

The primary tradeoff of the i2.2xlarge is its older CPU architecture, which lacks AVX-512, AMX, and modern vector extensions, resulting in weak performance for tasks like software compilation and LLM text generation. However, the inclusion of a 1600 GB local NVMe SSD and 61.0 GB of RAM makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-heavy workloads that do not require high-frequency compute. Appropriate workloads include database operations, static web serving, and legacy storage-intensive applications.
